/TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Issued at 119 AM MDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Our warm streak comes to a close Tuesday with cooler temperatures 
expected. The upper level shortwave passing north of our area ahead 
of the stalled upper level low will help push a cold front south. 
The cooler air is rather shallow and will have a hard time pushing 
past the Laramie Ranges. Locations along and east of I-25 should see 
about a 10 to 15 degree drop in afternoon temperatures compared to 
Monday, while further west a modest 5 degree drop is expected. The 
trends from yesterday are towards a more substantial cold front that 
stalls further south, thus pushing the axis of best theta-e 
advection southward into Colorado. This will be the favored corridor 
for heavier convective rainfall when the upper level system 
approaches. Scattered showers pass through the area through the day 
post front due to isentropic lift ahead of the upper level low. Not 
much rainfall from these showers, but a dreary and cloudy day can be 
expected.

Overnight, better forcing begins to move in with the upper level 
systems arrival. The best opportunity for beneficial rainfall occurs 
Tuesday night through Wednesday. Grand ensembles have the best 
chances of rainfall in the western and southern portion of the area 
where the mean precipitation totals are between half an inch and an 
inch. If we manage to pull off some MUCAPE on our side of the 
system, a few thunderstorms or convectively enhanced showers may 
materialize to give locally higher amounts. The snow level should 
also be low enough on the western half of the system to allow 
elevations at or above about 8500 feet to see precipitation cross 
over to snow. This would let the peaks of the Sierra Madre and Snowy 
Ranges see snowfall. It is a little soon to talk about possible 
ranges of snowfall at the peaks given the wide envelope of amounts 
in ensembles currently.

After Wednesday we still have uncertainty in the evolution of the 
forecast. As mentioned in the previous few discussions the 
uncertainty lies in if the upper level system is picked up by a 
southeastward advancing clipper out of Canada. The consensus 
starting to resolve in different models and ensembles are towards 
the solution that the trough ejection that becomes the clipper 
occurs near Alaska and moves southeast. Still, there are a few 
models such as the ECMWF that keep the ridge to the north strong 
enough to block the clipper and instead the upper level system 
stalls and lingers over our area while decaying through the forecast 
period. This would keep temperatures more mild and give better 
chances of rainfall, but does appear to be the outlier solution in 
more recent model cycles. If we commit to the GFS, and a majority of 
ensemble solutions at this point, of the system being picked up by 
the clipper then we can expect a cold end to the forecast. As the 
upper level system departs the cold air behind it will be forced 
southeast by a strong ridge. Gusty winds may accompany the cold air 
over the plains regions. Friday morning looks particularly chilly 
with perhaps the first widespread freeze of the season for a good 
portion of the area. Currently the likelihood of freezing 
temperatures from the Grand Ensemble for areas along and east of I-
25 are 20-40%, while west have a 50-80% chance. It is important to 
mention that a good number of the GEFS ensemble members are more 
aggressive with the progression of the trough that promotes these 
cold temperatures and are skewing the outcome of the Grand Ensemble 
towards the colder solutions. If we get a solution somewhere in the 
middle we could have a portion of the upper level trough elongate 
and stretch southwest while the majority gets swept up. A small 
chance this solution allows some upslope flow with the remaining 
moisture to create snow showers. Snow levels with be fairly low at 
around 6-5000 feet. Saturday morning looks also chilly as the 
western edge of the cold air mass lingers over the Panhandle. After 
the cold spell we warm up in the return flow post front Saturday and 
Sunday afternoons.
